correctness.rationale: If c=0 or the full ball minimizer is feasible, the output is exact. Otherwise write d0=-c/||c||, q=x+tau d0, and v=p-q. The support inequality gives n·d0>=0 when tau>0; if tau=0 and n·d0<0 the ray enters the rolling ball, a contradiction. The relaxed solution is in the tangent plane (the unconstrained solution is outside the halfspace or on its boundary). Since q is feasible for the relaxation, d0·v>=0 for every minimizer, including a tie. Hence s^2>=||p-x||^2=||v||^2+tau^2+2tau d0·v>=||v||^2. Projection into the tangent ball is feasible in K, does not increase distance to q, and moves by a nonpositive multiple of v+rho n, whose scalar product with q-x is nonnegative. Expanding the two distances to x proves locality. The excess objective is bounded by ||c|| times the exact displacement sqrt(rho^2+||v||^2)-rho, giving both displayed bounds. On the disk, at x=rho e1 and s=rho eps, the positive tangential component eps^3 forces the unique relaxed solution x+s e2; the disk support point rho d_eps lies in the local ball since its squared distance to x is at most 2rho^2 eps^6. The repaired support gap is rho(1-(sqrt(1-eps^6)+eps^4)/sqrt(1+eps^2))=rho eps^2/2+O(rho eps^4). Thus the uniform coefficient cannot be reduced. The supplied disk tests were inspected, not run; their tolerances and finite scope do not bear the proof.
residual_risks: The stronger radius-dependent upper bound is not certified pointwise optimal at fixed s. This is an exact-geometry result, not an inexact implementation or tie-breaking stability analysis.
